MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 8, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:00
p.m., on October 8, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 3, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Mayor Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel ~ Anticipated Litigation. Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: Two potential cases.

 RECESS AND RECONVENE THE MEETING

 At the hour of 5:01 pm Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Mayor Kelley
 reconvened the meeting at 6:05 pm with all Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  October 8, 2024
  City Attorney Curley announced the City Council was updated on closed session item, and there are
 no reportable actions.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  2024 Walk Against Drugs

  Received presentation from Crime Prevention Specialist TJ Robertson.

 P2.  Proclaim October 6 through October 12, 2024, To Be Fire Prevention Week

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamation to Fire Chief Cheyne Maule.

 P3.  La Paz Widening

  Received presentation from Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Brianna Jokerst, M.V.; Introduced herself as the Club Leader of the Trabuco Trailblazers 4-H
 Club, a Mission Veijo based club. She mentioned 4-H is a national non-profit youth
 development program, providing opportunities to develop leadership, citizenship, and life skills
 through experiential learning. She added, the week of October 7 – 12, is National 4-H week
 and provided their website for additional information https://trabuco4h.com/.

 Giovanni Hubnik, M.V.; A senior at CVHS and member of the Community of Character
 Committee. He introduced the character trait for the month of October “Respect” and gave
 examples of being respectful in everyday life. Lastly, he concluded by quoting John Whitten
 “Respect a man and he will do all the more”.

 Kade Schenewerk, M.V.; Stated he is a member of the Trabuco Trailblazers 4-H Club, that he
 raised a 4-H lamb, and had fun participating in the 4-H auction at the Orange County Fair.

 Kai Schenewerk, M.V.; Stated he is also a member of the Trabuco Trailblazers 4-H Club.
 Shared that he raised a 4-H pig, and that he has learned a lot and enjoys his time at the club.

 Tom Moore, M.V.; Referenced a resident requesting the renaming of Barcelona Park at the last
 Council Meeting and suggested the possibility of establishing a memorial wall to be designated
 at a specific park, as an option. He also voiced his concerns with regards to the widening of
 La Paz Road.

City Council Minutes  2  October 8, 2024
  Audrey Nguyen, Lake Forest; Announced that she has been a member of the Trabuco
 Trailblazers 4-H Club for the past six years. She spoke of projects and competitions she has
 participated in, and that she is looking forward to attending the state leadership conference.

 Iris Nguyen, Lake Forest; Shared that she too is a member of the Trabuco Trailblazers 4-H
 Club. She listed some of her favorite projects and events, and how 4-H encourages confidence,
 leadership, and public speaking skills.

 Mike Maiolo, M.V.; Thanked the Council for opportunity to share an upcoming event “Love
 Mission Viejo” this coming Saturday, October 12, from 9-Noon. Shared that 450 people have
 registered to participate in one of the 27 projects within the city. He concluded by recognizing
 a small group of individuals who dedicated their time to help make this event possible.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Items 10, 11, 12, and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

 Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, to approve the
 Consent Calendar outlined below.

 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 24, 2024, as
  presented.

 2.  General Check Register Dated September 13, 2024, in the Amount of $992,324.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  General Check Register Dated September 20, 2024, in the Amount of $1,422,983.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Golf Check Register Dated September 13, 2024, in the Amount of $274,237.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated September 20, 2024, in the Amount of $9,072.08

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  October 8, 2024
  6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2024

  Received and filed.

 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2024

  Received and filed.

 8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2024

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2024

  Received and filed.

 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 10. Budget Adjustment in the Amount of $98,000 for the Senior Mobility Program

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented a brief overview.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt Resolution
  24-47 approving Transportation Services with the Senior Mobility Program and increase the
  Program Budget by $98,000 using available Measure M2 Grant Funding.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 11. High-Intensity Activated Crosswalk (HAWK) Traffic Signal Installation & Intersection
  Improvements (CIP 24259)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented a brief overview.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
  the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer, and authorize
  staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

City Council Minutes  4  October 8, 2024
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 12. Orange County Transportation Authority 2024-2025 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented a brief overview.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt Resolution
  24-48 approving the Submittal of the La Paz Road Corridor and Cabot Road Corridor
  Improvement Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for Funding
  Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program
  (Project P); (2) adopt Resolution 24-49 approving the Submittal of the Alicia
  Parkway/Olympiad Road Intersection Improvement Project to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA) for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional
  Capacity Program (Project O); and (3) direct staff to transmit Resolutions to OCTA, in
  conjunction with the City's funding applications for said projects.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 13. High-Intensity Activated Crosswalk (HAWK) Traffic Signal Installation & Intersection
  Improvements (CIP 24259)

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 24-50 approving the City of Mission Viejo's Local Hazard Mitigation Plan; and (2)
  adopt Resolution 24-51 establishing Certain Positions as Authorized Agents to Apply for
  Disaster Assistance Funding.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  October 8, 2024
  MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 14.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received written report.

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 No report given.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 No report given.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 15.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum commenced by giving a brief overview of the ULI (Urban Land Institute)
The California Insurance Drought presentation she attended, the impact it is having on the State and
encouraged residents to contact Governor Newsom’s Office. She also attended the Shred Event, at the
very last minute, and was glad to see the truck was not full. She complemented and thanked Waste
Management for the great work they are doing. She spoke of upcoming events; Love Mission Viejo
and OCFA Open Houses 2024, both on Saturday, October 12, Tee it Up Fore Marines Golf Tournament
at Camp Pendleton on Friday, October 18, Walk Against Drugs and Fright Night Themed Night Market
on Saturday, October 19, and lastly Pumpkin Drive at Sierra Recreation Center on Sunday, October 20.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell spoke of the Nadadores, and the various swim meets that took place this past
weekend. He also mentioned the Sports and Economic Tourism Committee met with a French
Company, that represented/assisted approximately 106 different teams in the Paris Olympics, and
toured Misson Viejo with them. Lastly, Council Member Goodell shared that the Dutch shall be visiting
Mission Viejo at the beginning of November to solidify plans for the next couple of years leading up
to the 2028 Olympics.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated she had the opportunity of being Principal for the Day at Viejo
Elementary School, which she enjoyed, and looks forward to again next year. She added that
Capistrano Unified School District is looking to double the participation next year, and that community
City Council Minutes  6  October 8, 2024
 members are also able to participate by just signing up. She also attended the Bathgate Elementary
School Character Awards and is participating in their Walk to School Day event tomorrow.

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch announced the upcoming Subterranean Soundscapes: Halloween Spooky
acapella concert taking place next Wednesday, October 16, in the Jeronimo Tunnel along Oso Creek
Trail. He attended the Mission Viejo Animal Services Open House celebrating 30 years of service and
donated a pin from the Paris Olympic Games towards the time capsule. He also had the opportunity of
being Principal for the Day, at Castille Elementary School, an incredible program, where he witnessed
the fourth and fifth graders elect their council leaders. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch shared his
attendance at the OCFA Girls Empowerment Camp, a two-day program giving women the opportunity
to see what it would be like to choose a career as a firefighter.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley stated she attended the following events; Vocational Visions Board Meeting and
presented them with a proclamation in honor of their 50th Anniversary, the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast
in Irvine, an inspirational and well attended event by Mayors and community members, the Mission
Viejo Christian School Award Ceremony for their achievement in receiving the 2024 National Blue
Ribbon Award, the Raise Craze event at Riley Elementary School, National Coffee With A Cop at
Philz Coffee with Captain Ivins and his Deputies, Principal for the Day, at Capistrano Valley High
School, where she interacted with many students and teachers, and lastly the Mission Viejo Animal
Services Open House celebrating 30 years of service and recognizing the great work they provide to
all five cities. Mayor Kelley asked Fire Chief Maule to confirm which Fire Stations shall be
participating in the Fire Station Open House this coming Saturday. He announced Station 40 in Coto
de Caza, Station 7 in San Juan Capistrano, Station 45 in Rancho Santa Margarita and Station 58 in
Ladera Ranch. He did add that next year Mission Viejo’s new station 24 shall be participating. She
encouraged residents to attend Love Mission Viejo Day on Saturday, October 12, and the Walk Against
Drugs event on Saturday, October 19. Mayor Kelley concluded by complementing Community of
Character speaker Giovanni Hubnik, she spoke of committee and what a great opportunity it is for
students seventh grade through high school, and to contact her for more information.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:34p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Marine Corps Veteran and Marines and Sailors Adoption
Committee Member Hugh Speed to Tuesday, October 22, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 22, 2024

City Council Minutes  7  October 8, 2024
